faq.q: What is the origin of Ghassan?
faq.a: Ghassan is associated with Arabic. Ghassan is the standard transliteration of غسّان (Ghassān), the Ghassanid tribal name. The source gloss 'fine, handsome' and the sibling record's 'strong, firm' are two different traditional explanations of a name whose deeper etymology is disputed; this is recorded at medium confidence and neither gloss should be treated as settled.
Yes — the underlying form غسان is Arabic.
Ghassan can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.a: In Urdu, Ghassan is rendered غسان and carries the sense خوبصورت، خوش شکل.

faq.q: What does Ghassan mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Ghassan is rendered غسان and carries the sense خوش‌رو، زیبا.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Ghassan, ghassan. Script forms are غسان, ग़स्सान.

faq.q: Is Ghassan a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
